# Help, a Finite Export and a Daemon

A synthetic tool has `export`, `serve`, `--help` and `--version` paths. This is a parser-independent
walkthrough, not a runnable program or a requirement to adopt a command package.

## Command Matrix

| Invocation | Dependencies | Lifecycle | Output |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `example-tool --help` | Static command metadata | No operational host | Usage text |
| `example-tool --version` | Build/version metadata | No operational host | Version |
| `example-tool export --limit 5` | Export service and selected source | Await finite command and cleanup | One versioned JSON result |
| `example-tool serve` | Selected runtime services | Host-owned daemon | Operational diagnostics |

Example configuration fragment:

```json
{
  "Export": {
    "Limit": 20
  }
}
```

If `--limit` is absent, effective limit is 20. If supplied as 5, it is 5. If supplied as zero,
the command reports validation failure rather than silently replacing it with a default.
The parser must retain explicit-option presence; a default limit generated by parsing must not
overwrite the configured value.

## Dispatch Outline

```text
Parse with the existing parser.
If parse fails, render its safe syntax diagnostic and return syntax failure.
If parser selects help/version, render metadata and return without operational DI.
Bind selected-command configuration and explicit CLI overrides; validate.
Build selected-command services.
Execute finite operation or daemon using its own lifecycle contract.
Await shutdown/disposal; map the final outcome to the documented process code.
```

For export, return success only after the result is complete and required cleanup finishes.
No unrelated hosted consumer starts. If export requires a hosted transport, explicitly start it
and follow the bounded cleanup steps from the reference.

## Example Exit Contract

These numbers are a **synthetic choice**, not a new fleet-wide standard. Preserve an existing
tool's contract or obtain approval before changing it.

| Outcome | Example code |
| --- | --- |
| Help/version or complete operation | 0 |
| Invalid syntax/options | 2 |
| Operational/startup/shutdown failure | 1 |
| User-requested cancellation | 3 |

## Process Acceptance Cases

| Case | Required result |
| --- | --- |
| Help/version with all integration configuration removed | Code 0; no client constructors, network calls or credential prompts |
| Invalid command/option | Code 2; safe stderr diagnostic; no operational side effects |
| Limit omitted versus explicitly supplied | Configuration 20 versus CLI 5 respectively |
| Export succeeds | Process terminates; stdout is exactly one valid result, without host logs |
| Source fails halfway | Code 1; no complete-success result representing partial data |
| Cancellation during export | Code 3; cancellation reaches source; cleanup still attempted |
| Work and shutdown both fail | Code 1; primary failure retained; secondary failure visible safely |
| Daemon background task faults | Verified nonzero process exit, not merely a shutdown log |

Use process timeouts and fake sources. A handler unit test returning `1` does not prove the
packaged entrypoint, shell wrapper or container returns `1`.
